To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glucocorticoids inhibit CYP1B induction via a mechanism involving suppression of transcriptional activation.
the glucocorticoids inhibit the aryl hydrocarbons receptor-regulated CYP1B expression in rat mammary and embryo fibroblastic cell cultures.
the AhR is a transcription factor that regulates the expression of the CYP1A1, CYP1A2, and CYP1B2 genes in the rat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of CYP1A1 and CYP1B2 by the AhR and glucocorticoid receptors.
the role of the AhR and its nuclear translocator in the control of CYP1b1 expression and the role of glucocorticoids in this regulation.
the mechanisms of TCDD-induced carcinogenesis in mammary epithelium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the AhR and glucocorticoid receptors are linked in a complex manner to the regulation of CYP1b1, which has implications for mammary gland development, carcinogenesis and the metabolism of xenobiotic compounds in the mammary tissue.
the AhR regulates expression of the CYP1 gene, but that glucocorticoids inhibit AhR activity in a manner that is independent of the AhR nuclear translocation.
glucocorticoids inhibit CYP1B expression in RMF and that this is mediated through a glucocorticoid response element.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glucocorticoids suppress AhR-regulated genes, but not AhR expression, and that the glucocorticoids may also affect cell growth.

glucocorticoids are potent inhibitors of TCDD induction of the CYP1A1 gene in rat mammary epithelial cells, but not of CYP1A2 in rat liver epithelial cells, or of the CYP2C gene in rat kidney epithelial cells.

glucocorticoids suppress AhR-regulated CYP1B expression via a mechanism independent of the glucocorticoids receptor, and that this mechanism may be linked to the antiproliferative effects of these hormones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glucocorticoids suppress CYP1B expression by a mechanism involving a rapid suppression of the CYP1A1 enhancer region.
glucocorticoids can inhibit CYP1B induction by TCDD, and that this inhibition occurs through the glucocorticoids' ability to bind to and activate their receptors.
CYP1B is regulated by the glucocorticoids in a manner similar to CYP1A1 and that this regulation may be a mechanism for the suppression of tumor promotion by glucocorticoid hormones.
